title: Article 8 — Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India

content.overview: Article 8 enables a person of Indian origin ordinarily residing outside India to be registered as a citizen of India by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in the country of residence, if the person (or either parent or any grandparent) was born in undivided India (Government of India Act, 1935 definition).
content.glance: Indian-origin person abroad: born (self/parent/grandparent) in undivided India → may be registered as citizen by Indian diplomatic/consular representative.
content.study:
Article 8 addresses the overseas Indian-origin population at commencement.

Conditions:
- Person is ordinarily resident outside India.
- Person, or either parent, or any grandparent, was born in India as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935 (as originally enacted).
- Registration by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in the country where the person is residing, in the form and manner prescribed.

Effect: such a registered person is entitled to citizenship rights under the Constitution.

Modern counterpart: registration and overseas citizenship frameworks under the Citizenship Act, 1955 (including OCI, which is not full citizenship). Article 8 itself is a commencement-era registration route.

Examination: state birth-in-undivided-India link (self/parent/grandparent); registration by diplomatic/consular officer; distinguish from OCI under the 1955 Act.

sections.heading: Key elements
sections.body:
1. Ordinary residence outside India.
2. Indian origin via birth of self, parent or grandparent in undivided India (GoI Act 1935).
3. Registration by Indian diplomatic or consular representative.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 8.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 8 provides that a person of Indian origin who is ordinarily residing outside India may be registered as a citizen of India by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in that country if the person, or either parent, or any grandparent was born in undivided India (as defined in the Government of India Act, 1935). It is a commencement-era overseas registration route; modern overseas status is largely under the Citizenship Act, 1955.

examTips: Birth link: self / parent / grandparent in undivided India; registration by diplomatic/consular officer.
content.migrationNote: QUAL remediation 2026-10-09: overseas Indian-origin registration clarified.

keyTakeaways: Art 8: overseas Indian-origin registration via diplomatic/consular representative.
